parsed.main_gap: The claim K≥1 always (at least one nonunit remains) is justified by a false general principle; the correct one-line reason (lcm(m,n)>1, so a move cannot kill both nonunits) is absent.

errors.description: Invalid justification that the number of nonunits never reaches 0. A nonincreasing positive integer sequence certainly can reach 0; the real reason is that a move on m,n>1 yields entries with product lcm(m,n)>1, so they cannot both equal 1. Trivially repairable, but as written the deduction that exactly one nonunit remains is unsupported.
errors.quote:
A nonnegative integer that
never increases and starts at a positive value can never reach \(0\); hence \(K\ge1\) at
every stage

parsed.notes: Termination via lexicographic (P,K) descent and the primewise Euclidean gcd invariant are both correct and cleanly argued; final formula M = ∏ p^{gcd of valuations} is right. Only one small logical slip mars an otherwise complete solution.
